definition: Assigning category labels to documents written in different languages, often transferring a classifier trained on one language to others.
details: Assigning category labels to documents written in different languages, often transferring a classifier trained on one language to others. It relies on cross-lingual embeddings or multilingual models so that label knowledge learned in a high-resource language generalizes to low-resource ones.

explainer.lead: Cross-lingual document classification lets a system sort documents by topic or category even when they are written in different languages. It can reuse labels learned from a language with plenty of training data to classify documents in languages with much less.

tiers.eli5: It is like reading a book in a language you barely know by relying on what you learned sorting books in a language you know well.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers rely on cross-lingual embeddings or multilingual models so label knowledge learned in a high-resource language generalizes to low-resource ones. A pitfall is weak transfer when the languages are linguistically distant.
tiers.paperLevel: Assigning category labels to documents written in different languages, often transferring a classifier trained on one language to others, relying on cross-lingual embeddings or multilingual models.

explainer.example: Train a classifier on English news articles labeled “sports” or “politics.” A Spanish article about a football match is encoded with the same multilingual model, and the classifier labels it “sports” without requiring a separate set of labeled Spanish articles.
explainer.intuition: Documents about the same topic can share a useful meaning-based representation even when their words come from different languages. A classifier can learn category boundaries in that shared space instead of starting over for every language.
howItWorks: Collect labeled documents in a high-resource source language.
Represent their text with cross-lingual embeddings or a multilingual model.
Train a classifier to map those representations to category labels.
Represent target-language documents in the same shared space.
Apply the classifier to predict their categories.
explainer.whyItMatters: It reduces the need to create labeled training data separately for every language. That is especially valuable for low-resource languages, where such data may be scarce.
misconceptions: It does not necessarily translate each document before classifying it.
It is not language identification: the output is a document category, not the document’s language.
Training in one language does not guarantee equally accurate classification in every other language.
